title: Annual plankton density tests gave uncertain thermal transfer on the Northeast Shelf
abstract: We tested whether annual density change retained the high thermal transfer reported for Northeast Shelf plankton. We used original NOAA EcoMon tows in 1992-2023. We averaged raw taxon densities over six seasons before taking logs. This preserves a fixed annual density total when it moves among seasons, with separate changes allowed for each taxon. In cells with at least three sampled years per season and half, transfer of early spatial temperature slopes was 0.603 for 39 zooplankton groups and 1.019 for 37 fish-larva taxa. Nominal 95% crossed-bootstrap intervals were 0.119-1.198 and 0.050-2.308. Conservative 97.5% intervals, used for two primary tests, were -0.017 to 1.371 and -0.226 to 3.661. A four-year coverage rule reduced the estimates to 0.293 and 0.857 and changed geographic support. Fish occurrence transfer was weaker and uncertain. Annual integration kept positive point estimates but did not establish positive or full transfer after the two-test allowance. Sparse visits within seasons, few spatial blocks, surface temperature and non-thermal spatial gradients limit inference. The results do not identify dispersal or demographic response as the cause. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external-data reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Annual transfer depends on seasonal coverage. Intervals are nominal 95% crossed-bootstrap limits. Primary species changes are shown against their early spatial temperature predictions.

citations.reason: We reuse its preparation code and test its marine thermal-transfer contrast with annual taxon densities.
Its seasonal direction test left separate taxon timing shifts open. We test annual integrated density.
The low cross-network thermal transfer motivates the marine contrast.
